questions.q: In "Find a product with a supplier and a buyer Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Ask what they would change: price, quantity, speed.
Give peers feedback.
Show currency and the exchange rate you used, with the date.
Choose one product you can understand and test (for example packaged food items or hand tools).

questions.q: In "Trade documents Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Quote: what you offer and at what price. Order: what the buyer accepts.
Give peers feedback.
Get three supplier quotes and two buyer needs: price, quantity, time.
Classification codes decide duty; use official tariff lists for your country.

questions.q: In "Choose terms and cost the deal Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Standard international terms split cost and risk between seller and buyer. Pick one and write why.
Payment terms: advance, open account, bank guarantee; each changes risk.
Commercial invoice: what is sold, quantity, price, currency, terms.
Transport document: proof the goods were handed to the carrier. Certificate of origin: where goods come from.

questions.q: In "Customs, payment and compliance Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep the file in order with a contents list.
Know your walk-away price before you talk.
Exchange-rate risk: a 5% swing can remove your margin.
Never promise delivery you cannot control.

questions.q: In "Run the mock trade file Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Identify three risks and what you will do about each.
Licences and sanctions: check before any deal; some destinations are not allowed.
Choose one product you can understand and test (for example packaged food items or hand tools).
Take the check.

questions.q: In "Margins, pricing and negotiation Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Enquiry → quote → order → invoice → packing list → shipping plan.
Exchange-rate risk: a 5% swing can remove your margin.
Licences and sanctions: check before any deal; some destinations are not allowed.
Never promise delivery you cannot control.
